claims.text: Rapid thermal annealing after fabrication will reduce compositional segregation in cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi relative to samples without post-processing.
Rapid thermal annealing after fabrication will relieve residual thermal stresses in cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi.
Rapid thermal annealing after fabrication will lower defect density in cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi.
Conventionally bulk- or additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi exhibits significant compositional segregation.
Conventionally bulk- or additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi exhibits significant residual thermal stresses.
Conventionally bulk- or additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi contains processing-induced defects.
The proposed intervention is a precisely temperature-controlled, high-temperature, short-dwell annealing cycle applied immediately after fabrication.
Keeping annealing within the alloy's thermal stability range can prevent grain coarsening and undesired phase transformations.
Brief high-temperature exposure enhances atomic diffusion in AlCrFeNiSi.
Enhanced atomic diffusion during rapid annealing homogenizes the AlCrFeNiSi microstructure.
Brief high-temperature exposure promotes relaxation of thermal stresses.
Recovery processes enabled by rapid thermal annealing reduce defect density.
Reduced segregation, residual stress, and defect density will improve the mechanical integrity of AlCrFeNiSi.
The proposed effect applies under customary additive-manufacturing or bulk-fabrication conditions if annealing parameters avoid adverse phase changes.
